lead: A DRAM lawsuit clears a pleading hurdle, which is not a verdict on collusion. Enterprise AI measurement and precision robotics attract funding, while chip-access and political reports remain limited to excerpts.

sections.title: Explicit loops and configurable endpoints
sections.intro: A robotics programming argument and a small Datasette release favor visible control boundaries.

sections.title: Power contracts and voting power
sections.intro: Two inaccessible reports describe different constraints on AI infrastructure and company control.

sections.title: Plausibility is not a verdict
sections.intro: A memory-market lawsuit advances while chip-access reporting remains excerpt-based.

sections.title: Measure outcomes and train precise tasks
sections.intro: Enterprise analytics and industrial robots pursue different forms of applied value.

sections.title: What a representation does not prove
sections.intro: Model geometry, licensing arguments and separate account configurations need precise boundaries.

sections.title: Making and performing with AI
sections.intro: A physical clock offers a detailed build record; video and event snippets provide much less.

sections.title: Reading the financial narrative
sections.intro: Interpretations of chip demand and an IPO prospectus should remain interpretations.
